source.title: Functional neurological restoration of amputated peripheral nerve using biohybrid regenerative bioelectronics

material: Parylene-C MEA with PEDOT:PSS electrodes carrying fibrin hydrogel layer with human iPSC-derived skeletal myocytes

formulation.evidence: Final concentrations are as follows: FG = 3.125, 6.25, 12.5, and 25 mg/ml; Th = 1 U/ml; and CaCl2 = 20 mM.

processing.evidence: by slowly dissolving fibrinogen (F8630, Sigma-Aldrich) for 2 hours at 37°C (solution named SOL-FG)
They were seeded onto devices with densities of 100,000 cells/cm2
The devices are plasma-treated at 25 W for 1 min to make the surface hydrophilic for cell culture.

duration_days.evidence: implanted human iPSC-derived myocytes can survive in a rat model for up to 28 days

biology.species: human cells in athymic nude rat

culture_days.evidence: mature multinucleated myotubes are formed on the surface of the biohybrid device by day 8

other_outcomes.evidence: [weeks 1 to 4: 12.9-, 11.3-, 19.7-, and 32.0-dB mean signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), respectively]
other_outcomes.name: mean SNR of nerve recordings, weeks 1 to 4

notes: Device sutured to transected forearm nerve bundle (ulnar and median) and placed subcutaneously above latissimus dorsi in immunodeficient rats for 4 weeks. Cell survival shown qualitatively (no percentages stated).
